description_full: Nippon Express Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides logistics services in Japan, the Americas, Europe, East Asia, South Asia, and Oceania. The company offers railway forwarding, motor cargo transportation, air freight forwarding, harbor transportation, warehousing, in-factory work, information asset management, and real estate rental services; and heavy haulage and construction. It also involved in the provision of security guard services; sale of distribution equipment, wrapping and packaging materials, vehicles, petroleum, and liquefied petroleum gas; vehicle maintenance; insurance agency; mediation; planning, designing and management of real estate properties; investigation and research; logistics finance; and employee dispatching business. The company was formerly known as Nippon Express Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Nippon Express Holdings, Inc. in January 2022. Nippon Express Holdings, Inc. was founded in 1872 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: NIPPON EXPRESS HLDGS INC is a mid-cap industrials business with a $7.8B market cap on $16.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 10% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $966M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 83.60× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -9.2% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 2.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.2×.

Shareholder yield of 2.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 8.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
